title: The Wright Brothers
summary: Josh and Chuck profile the Wright brothers, Wilbur and Orville, covering their childhood and family (including sister Catherine), their bicycle shop in Dayton, Ohio, and their glider experiments at Kitty Hawk. They build a wind tunnel and their own lift and drag tables, correcting Smeaton's coefficient, then design a powered flyer with a hip-cradle control system and a homemade aluminum engine. The episode covers the first powered flight on December 17 (Orville's turn, after Wilbur's failed attempt), the slow press response, the French challengers, the 1908 European demonstrations, Selfridge's fatal crash, Wilbur's death from typhoid, and Orville's and Catherine's later lives. It ends with a listener mail asking for a Titanic episode.

segments.title: Opening banter on the Wright brothers
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open by saying a Wright brothers biopic is overdue and mention a short film starring Tony Hale. They frame the brothers as self-taught bike shop owners who became the first to achieve powered flight.

segments.title: Family background and the brothers' bond
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Wright family of seven children, with five reaching adulthood, and their parents Milton and Susan. They discuss Wilbur and Orville's close lifelong partnership, Wilbur's hockey injury and depression, and Catherine's role as the only sibling to graduate college.

segments.title: Bike shop and the decision to build a flying machine
segments.summary: The brothers open a bike shop in Dayton, Ohio, with Catherine managing it. Wilbur writes to the Smithsonian, and Secretary Samuel Langley sends them reference material. They study Otto Lilienthal's data and identify aircraft control as the central problem.

segments.title: Wing warping and early kite experiments
segments.summary: Wilbur gets the idea for wing warping from a bent cardboard box. They test box-kite-style gliders with wires controlling the wings, then turn to weather data and choose Kitty Hawk, North Carolina for its wind and sandy landings.

segments.title: Glider crashes, wind tunnel and Smeaton's coefficient
segments.summary: A 1900 glider fails to lift a passenger, and the 1901 glider crashes with Wilbur aboard. The brothers doubt earlier data, build a wind tunnel and about 200 model wings with homemade balances, and revise Smeaton's coefficient.

segments.title: Mid-episode break
segments.summary: Short ad break before the discussion of powering the aircraft.

segments.title: Propellers, engine, and hip-cradle controls
segments.summary: The brothers carve propellers and realize they work like wings turned vertically. Charlie Taylor builds an aluminum four-cylinder engine of about twelve horsepower. Bicycle chains drive counter-rotating propellers, and a hip cradle with wires controls warping, rudder, and elevators. The plane launches from a rail.

segments.title: First powered flight and the press response
segments.summary: Wilbur's first attempt on December 17 crashes after the elevators break. Orville makes the first controlled powered flight of about twelve seconds, and Wilbur later flies 852 feet. A gust then destroys the flyer. Their press release gets little response, and John Culver's article in Gleanings in Bee Culture is the first published account.

segments.title: European competition and the 1908 demonstrations
segments.summary: Santos-Dumont and Henri Farman are presented as French rivals who flew in Europe. Wilbur flies in France in August 1908 and impresses the French. Katherine helps negotiate an army contract, and the brothers become celebrities.

segments.title: Selfridge crash, Wilbur's death, and later lives
segments.summary: Thomas Selfridge dies in a 1908 crash with Orville, who survives. Wilbur dies of typhoid in 1912 at age 45. Orville sells the company, lives at Hawthorne Hill, and stops speaking to Catherine after her marriage. She dies of pneumonia, and Orville dies three days after a heart attack.

segments.title: Listener mail from Quinn about a Titanic episode
segments.summary: A ten-year-old listener named Quinn asks for a Titanic episode. The hosts say one is planned.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the episode and give the contact address for listener mail.
